tasks.title: Repo-kind-aware planning lock + harness-source marker
tasks.objective: Make the planning lock repo-kind-aware in pre_tool_use.py. Add a shared is_harness_source_repo(root) (marker .factory/harness-source.json exists); when true, treat factory/, constitution/, harness/, .claude/, .codex/ as product while docs/, plans/, .factory/, prototype/, .github/ and root files stay exempt in both repo kinds. Allowlist the marker for .factory/ writes and commit it. Downstream gate + claim_files logic is unchanged (fixes the quickfix zero-scope report for free).
acceptance_criteria: In the harness repo (marker present), a raw Edit/Write and a Bash redirect under factory/ are DENIED when plan_status is not approved and no quickfix is open; ALLOWED once plan_status=approved and decomposition recorded.
In a client repo (no marker), the same factory/ write is ALLOWED, exactly as today.
A harness-repo quickfix touching factory/ paths claims them against the 5-file budget; the closed ledger reports the real files (not []), and the 6th over-budget write is refused.
A freshly scaffolded/vendored client carries no .factory/harness-source.json, so it classifies as a client.
docs/, plans/, .factory/, prototype/, .github/ and exempt root files stay writable in the harness repo (no over-locking).
verify_commands: uv run --with pytest python -m pytest factory/tests/test_gates.py -q -k "harness_repo or client_repo or quickfix or scaffolded_client or factory_state or planning_lock or bash_write_guard or bash_side_door"
tasks.reviewer_focus: Fail-safe direction (missing marker => client behavior, never lock a client); no over-locking of docs/plans/.github/root files; marker excluded from all vendoring; downstream claim_files path actually reached for machinery writes.
